channel.title: Wisconsin Newspaper Association - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Newspaper Association (wnanews.com)

item.title: CFINR award entries due February 16
item.description: Now in its third year, the Center for Integrity in News Reporting Awards will present six $25,000 cash prizes, including a new category for Investigative Reporting, alongside awards for Print, Broadcast, Cable Network, Digital Reporting, and reporting by members of the White House Correspondents’ Association.

item.title: ‘Cutting Through the Noise’ scheduled for March 31 in LaCrosse
item.description: UW-LaCrosse, Viterbo University and Western Technical College present “Cutting Through the Noise: A Call for Civil Discourse,” from 3:30-5 p.m. on Tuesday, March 31 at The Lunda Center at Western Technical College, 333 7th St. North in LaCrosse.

item.title: Andy Pennington to succeed George Stanley as Wisconsin Watch CEO
item.description: Wisconsin Watch, Wisconsin's statewide nonprofit news organization, will come under new leadership March 2 when Andy Pennington succeeds retiring CEO George Stanley.

item.title: Civil rights complaint filed against school board member
item.description: A civil rights complaint has been filed with the United States Department of Justice Civil Rights Division against Clintonville School Board President Glen Drew Lundt by district resident Michael Engel.

item.title: Baldwin Bulletin marks 150th anniversary
item.description: The Baldwin Bulletin was first published on October 18, 1873 — one year before the Village of Baldwin was officially incorporated.

item.title: State payments rise; municipal service costs increase more
item.description: State policymakers provided the largest funding increase on record in 2025 for a program that reimburses municipalities to provide services to state facilities such as colleges, universities, or prisons.

item.title: Senators use paper ballots, skip public debate
item.description: Wisconsin Senate committees — controlled by Republicans in the majority — are increasingly using paper ballots instead of meeting publicly in person to debate and vote on bills.

item.title: Former Crawford County Independent & Kickapoo Scout journalist earns Devroy Fellowship
item.description: Ambrosia Wojahn, who worked at The Crawford County Independent & Kickapoo Scout while attending Laurel High School in Viroqua, has been chosen as the winner of the Ann Devroy Fellowship.

item.title: Journal Sentinel to host March 7 panel discussion about guns
item.description: The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel will co-sponsor an open panel discussion about guns at 10 a.m. on March 7 at Most Worshipful Prince Hall Grand Lodge State of Wisconsin at Prince Hall Masonic Temple, which is located at 1218 W. North Ave. on Milwaukee’s north side.

item.title: WisEye bill clears Assembly but faces competing bill in Senate
item.description: Bipartisan legislation to give WisconsinEye, the state’s version of C-SPAN, taxpayer funds to publicly broadcast state government functions unanimously cleared the state Assembly on Tuesday, Feb. 10.
